Bill.BriefDescription: Providing a business and occupation tax credit for newly hired aerospace apprentices.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to providing a business and occupation tax creditfor newly hired aerospace apprentices; and adding a new section tochapter 82.04 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 82.04 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Beginning August 1, 2011, a credit is allowed against any taxdue under this chapter for new qualified employment positions createdat an eligible business subject to the conditions and requirements ofthis section. (2) The credit equals five thousand dollars for each new qualifiedemployment position with benefits and wages that provide wagecompensation as defined by state registered standards ofapprenticeship. The benefits must include a health care plan. (3) The credit may be claimed beginning in the reporting period inwhich the new qualified employment position is created; however, theemployment position must be maintained for at least the eightconsecutive full calendar quarters after the calendar quarter during p. 1 HB 1682which the qualified employment position is created as provided insubsection (10)(c)(iii) of this section. (4) The department must keep a running total of all credits allowedunder this section during each fiscal year. The department may notallow any credits which would cause the total to exceed two hundredfifty thousand dollars in any fiscal year. If all or part of a creditis disallowed under this subsection, the disallowed portion may becarried over into subsequent fiscal years until used; however, thecarryover into the next fiscal year is only permitted to the extentthat the cap for the next fiscal year is not exceeded. (5) A person may not claim a credit under this section in excess oftwo thousand five hundred dollars per employee in any calendar year.The credit may be used against any tax due under this chapter, and maybe carried over until used. No refunds may be granted for creditsunder this section. (6) No application is necessary for the tax credit. The person issubject to all of the requirements of chapter 82.32 RCW. (7) If at any time the department finds that a person is noteligible for tax credit under this section, the amount of taxes forwhich a credit has been claimed is immediately due. The departmentmust assess interest, but not penalties, on the taxes for which theperson is not eligible. The interest must be assessed at the rateprovided for delinquent excise taxes under chapter 82.32 RCW, isretroactive to the date the tax credit was taken, and accrues until thetaxes for which a credit has been used are repaid. (8) A person claiming the credit under this section must file acomplete annual report with the department under RCW 82.32.534. (9) A person may not claim a credit under this section if anotherstate excise tax credit has been claimed for the same employmentposition. (10) The following definitions apply throughout this section,unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (a) "Eligible business" means a business subject to the tax rateunder RCW 82.04.260(10). (b) "Health care plan" means any "employee welfare benefit plan" asdefined by the employee retirement income security act of 1974, 29U.S.C. Sec. 1001 et seq., and any "health plan" or "health benefitplan" as defined in RCW 48.43.005, for the purpose of providing for its HB 1682 p. 2 employees or their beneficiaries, through the purchase of insurance orotherwise, health care services. For the purposes of this section,"health care services" means services offered or provided by healthcare facilities and health care providers relating to the prevention,cure, or treatment of illness, injury, or disease. (c)(i) "Qualified employment position" means a position filled bya permanent fulltime apprentice. (ii) For purposes of this subsection (10)(c), "full time" means anormal work week of at least thirtyfive hours. (iii) Once a permanent, fulltime employee has been employed, aposition does not cease to be a qualified employment position solelydue to periods in which the position goes vacant, as long as: (A) The cumulative period of any vacancies in that position is notmore than one hundred twenty days in the eightquarter period; and (B) During a vacancy, the employer is actively recruiting areplacement permanent, fulltime employee for the position.
